definition: Caching responses keyed by embedding similarity of requests, so paraphrases of previously answered questions skip the model entirely.
details: Caching responses keyed by embedding similarity of requests, so paraphrases of previously answered questions skip the model entirely. Effective for support and FAQ-heavy traffic; requires careful thresholds and invalidation to avoid serving stale or subtly wrong answers.

explainer.lead: Semantic caching stores responses keyed by embedding similarity of requests, so paraphrases of previously answered questions skip the model entirely. It matters for support and FAQ-heavy traffic, but needs careful thresholds and invalidation to avoid stale or subtly wrong answers.

tiers.eli5: Like a help desk that recognizes a reworded version of a question it already answered and reuses that answer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers embed incoming requests, match them against cached request embeddings by similarity, and return the stored response above a threshold. A pitfall is that loose thresholds serve subtly wrong answers, and cache entries can go stale.
tiers.paperLevel: Responses are cached and keyed by embedding similarity between requests; a request whose similarity to a cached request exceeds a threshold skips the model. Correctness depends on threshold choice and invalidation policy.

explainer.example: A customer asks a reworded version of a common FAQ, and the system returns the cached answer because its embedding is close enough to the stored request.
